submission.justification: The project documents contain no humidity-ageing data for any candidate, so the hard transparency constraint is unverified for all three. R1 gives the best separation (about 4.6 sigma at 3 cm in the 2025 summary) but is an untreated porous radiator, so it is the most likely to be hygroscopic. I did not rerun R1 at 3 cm. R2 is porous with a hydrophobic treatment, which makes it the most plausible way to get good separation while meeting the humidity limit. Its separation peaks near 3 cm: 3.2 sigma at 1 cm, 3.45 at 2, 3.94 at 3, 3.72 at 4 and 2.69 at 6. This is a provisional recommendation. Before committing, someone must obtain 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing results (transparency loss of 10% or less) for R2. If R2 fails, R3 is the fallback. If R1 turns out to pass, it would be better at 3 cm.

requirements.requirement: Best possible pi/K separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R2 at 3 cm gives 3.94 sigma, the best thickness for R2. R1 would give more (4.6 sigma at 3 cm per the 2025 summary) but its humidity behaviour is unknown and likely worse.
No humidity-ageing data exists in any project document. The hydrophobic treatment on R2 suggests it should do well, but this is an inference, not a measurement.

requirements.requirement: Radiator is one of the three candidates
